cap_raised_from_the_worst_rate.why_the_mean_is_the_wrong_statistic: W988 itself measured that the spread is at least 1.9x and NOT monotonic in size. A limit chosen from the mean of a quantity like that fails exactly on the largest thing you own -- and the largest thing is where the measurement matters most.
cap_raised_from_the_worst_rate.new_basis: the WORST observed rate and the largest design in the corpus

measured_lower_bound_that_triggered_it.note: a LOWER bound -- the run had not returned when this was written

cap_raised_from_the_worst_rate.rule_followed: W823: raise a limit on a CHANGED MEASUREMENT, never because something failed. The measurement changed.
cap_raised_from_the_worst_rate.env_override: T27_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S, so the next wave to meet the cap does not have to rebuild the compiler to test whether the cap is the problem

bench_gate_deferred_again.why: scripts/tri has been executing the sweep across both waves; editing a running bash script risks corrupting its parse mid-run
bench_gate_deferred_again.note: recorded rather than quietly dropped -- a deferral with a reason is a plan, a deferral without one is a leak
